**Regression signs:** drop in groundedness after changing model or chunking; increase in editing rate in confirmations (the collection worsened); increase in staggering by “I did not understand”; increase in cost by intention without resolution gain; increasing average age of the quoted content (curacy stopped).

The readiness of a *site* to be read by agents, on another scale, is the theme of [Agent Ready](https://mauricio.issei.com.br/en/agent-ready).

Critical questions

#### Thirty questions in five groups

Each answer brings the conclusion and the seal that says how much it sustains itself. Open the door; the rest is collected.

##### 1 · Experience, protocols and interface (1 to 8)

**1. What differentiates a modern intranet from an EXP?**

**[INFERENCE]**

The intranet informs and forwards; the EXP executes and follows. The intranet organizes pages and audiences and measures reach; EXP organizes services and journeys on registration systems, measures resolution and effort and maintains the context of the collaborator in various channels.

**2. Does an EXP need to be composable?**

**[INFERENCE]**

Not necessarily. Componibility is paid for with many domains, many channels and strategy to exchange suppliers. For agents, the real requirement is that capabilities are exposed by contract: a suite with good APIs serves better than a complicable architecture without stable contracts.

**3. Is MACH an architectural requirement or possible strategy?**

**[RECOMMENDATION]**

Possible strategy. API-first and headless are for agents; microservices only where there is organizational border. It is worth remembering that the MACH Alliance is an association of suppliers, and its material is market positioning.

**4. Where does AG-UI really fit?**

**[FATO]**

Between the agent runtime and the application the user operates. MCP connects agent and tools, A2A connects agents, AG-UI connects agent to user. It doesn't fit into integration with registration systems or authorization.

**5. AG-UI is a protocol of UI, integration or interaction?**

**[FATO]**

Interaction. The documentation describes it as the connection of bidirectional runtime between agent and application and distinguishes it from the specifications of generative IU. It doesn't define components or connect systems.

**6. What is the relationship between AG-UI and generative UI?**

**[FATO]** **[INFERENCE]**

Channel and vocabulary. Generative UI specifications define *What?* render; AG-UI transports these orders to the client and brings the actions back. In practice, AG-UI frontend tools can request the rendering of catalog components.

**7. How to preserve determinism in a generative interface?**

**[RECOMMENDATION]**

Determinism where it matters, adaptation in the rest. They are deterministic: the rendering of each component, the validation of props, the execution of actions and components of confirmation and legal notice. They are adaptive and restricted: the choice of the component within the catalogue, the explanatory text and the composition within templates. High volume intentions use fixed templates; the free composition stays for the long tail.

**8. How does a system design become consumable by agents?**

**[RECOMMENDATION]**

Turning components into typed and described tools into a Component Registry: description of when to use and not to use; JSON Pros schema; issued actions and side effect; required context; component accessibility audit; standardized tokens (the format of the W3C Design Tokens Community Group has been stable since October 2025); and assessments that verify whether the agent chooses the right component.

##### 2 · Knowledge and search (9 to 11)

**9. What is the relationship between ECM, CSP, headless, search and RAG?**

**[INFERENCE]**

A chain in which each link inherits the quality of the former and cannot correct it. ECM keeps governed records; CSP exposes them as services; headless structure experience content for various channels; the search finds the right passage for the right person; the RAG generates the reasoned answer.

**10. What needs to be structured before implementing RAG?**

**[RECOMMENDATION]**

Six blockers: canonical source by type of content; explicit and exportable permissions to the index; status and validity; owner of each content; classification of information with rule of use by AI; evaluation set with real questions. Taxonomy, applicability metadata, section structure, life cycle events and deduplication are strongly recommended.

**11. How to implement and verify permission-aware retrieval?**

**[RECOMMENDATION]**

With permission prefilter in the index, using IdP-resolved identity: permissions as metadata for each chunk; filter in the query, never after the model saw the content; synchronization by events with propagation SLO; continuous leak tests with low privilege identities; overshare review before indexing.

##### 3 · Agents and integration (12 to 18)

**12. When does a chatbot stop being a chatbot and become an agent?**

**[INFERENCE]**

When you decide dynamically the next step, you use tools with effect and itera to the point. A bot that only responds, even with LLM, is chatbot or RAG. The distinction matters because the controls need to follow: whoever performs actions needs delegated identity, scope and HITL.

**13. What differentiates an agent from an automated workflow?**

**[FATO]** **[RECOMMENDATION]**

Who defines the sequence. In workflows, LLMs and tools are orchestrated by predefined code paths; in agents, LLM dynamically drives the process itself and the use of tools. Workflows gain in predictability and testability; agents gain in long tail flexibility. In regulated processes, prefer workflows with LLM steps.

**14. What is the role of MCP in this architecture?**

**[INFERENCE]**

Standard interface between agent and tool catalog, with specified authorisation model. Solve discovery, call schema, OAuth authorization in server access and trace propagation. It does not solve business rule, integration with systems, long processes or events. It requires audience validation and prohibits *token passthrough*. It is recommended to encapsulate the protocol, given the speed of change.

**15. What role does BFF play when agents have tools?**

**[RECOMMENDATION]**

Mold the capabilities for the channel agent: reduce payload and noise, aggregate frequent queries, normalize errors in explicit messages, impose pagination and limits, apply channel policy. BFF does not contain business rule; MCP defines *how* the tool is called, and the BFF, *What?* She gives it back.

**16. When to use API?**

**[INFERENCE]**

When the channel needs immediate response about the current state or wants to command an action whose acceptance can be decided on time. It is the default for most reading tools and commands that initiate processes. Wrong usage sign: long operations solved by synchronous call with high timeouts.

**17. When to use events?**

**[INFERENCE]**

When several consumers react to a fact that has already occurred, the producer should not know them and the reaction may be asynchronous: proactive notifications, reading projections, synchronization between systems, reindication triggers. Wrong usage sign: events used as request and response.

**18. When to use a workflow engine?**

**[RECOMMENDATION]**

When the process has been durable, human stages, timers, compensations or long duration. The agent starts the workflow with idempotence, consults the state and responds to user signals; never keeps the state of the process in the memory itself.

##### 4 · Identity, audit and exceptions (19 to 21)

**19. How to preserve identity and authorization during the execution of the agent?**

**[RECOMMENDATION]** **[FATO]**

Explicit delegation with composite identity, verified in each resource: the user authenticates in the experience; for each tool, the runtime gets a token by *token exchange* (subject = user, actor = agent, clan `act`, minimum scope, specific audience, according to RFC 8693); the tool servers validate the audience and do not pass the token; the final authorization happens at the point of the data; and the “whose” comes from the token, never from parameters generated by the model.

**20. How to audit a decision or action by an agent?**

**[RECOMMENDATION]**

With a task execution record, correlated with the registration system. The audit locates the execution by the transaction protocol, reconstructs the current context (instructions, sources and versions), verifies if the rule came from the domain and was not inferred by the model, confers subject, actor, scope and policy decision, verifies the explicit confirmation and allows the human review provided for in article 20 of the LGPD.

**21. How to deal with human exceptions?**

**[RECOMMENDATION]**

Treating exceptions as first class states of the process: each has type, queue with owner, SLA, structured context transferred and path to return to the flow. Present user confirmations use the interruption of AG-UI; third party approvals, a human task in the workflow engine.

##### 5 · Quality, operation and readiness (22-30)

**22. How to measure DEX when the interface is dynamic?**

**[RECOMMENDATION]**

Measuring by intention, not by screen: resolution by intention, time to resolution, perceived effort, shifts by resolution, editing rate in confirmations, abandonment by step, scaling and motive, recounted in 7 days — combined with the telemetry and feeling of DEX tools.

**23. How to test an interface that changes according to context?**

**[RECOMMENDATION]**

Testing components, contracts and behaviors, instead of fixed screens: components with unit tests, property-based testing and visual regression; all agent output validated against catalog schema; assessments with assertions on AG-UI events issued for each intention; replay of recorded flows with a simulated deterministic agent; accessibility by component and template.

**24. How to test agents?**

**[RECOMMENDATION]**

In layers, with statistical evaluations and regression in IC: tools (contract, idempotence, authorization); tool selection; acceptable trajectory; environment result with simulated systems; safety (red injection teaming, climbing and leakage); regression with thresholds for each model change, prompt or catalog; and continuous sampling evaluation in production.

**25. How to check accessibility in generative IU?**

**[RECOMMENDATION]**

Certifying components, not screens, and controlling dynamics: only audited components (WCAG 2.2 AA) enter the catalog; explicit focus management when the agent inserts or replaces components; moderate `aria-live`, with streaming announced per step; equivalent textual representation of each component; alternative navigation paths.

**26. How to preserve observability in agentic systems?**

**[RECOMMENDATION]**

Three-plan observability (services, agent, quality), with correlated dashes from end to end: OpenTelemetry with GenAI conventions; `traceparent` spread between agent and MCP servers; `RUN events_*` e `STEP_*` as anchors on the experience side; Quality and cost SLOs beyond availability and latency; personal data masked or in restricted storage.

**27. Which components should remain deterministic?**

**[RECOMMENDATION]**

Business rules and eligibility; authorization and policy decisions; execution of actions and their effects, with idempotence; process status; validation of UI entries and props; rendering of each component; components of confirmation, consent and legal notices; audit records; content life cycle (vigency, revocation, disposal).

**28. What components can be adaptive?**

**[RECOMMENDATION]**

Interpretation of intention; explanatory text and tone, within guardrails; choice and order of components within the catalogue and templates; suggestions for next steps; reformulation of search queries; sequence planning in low risk tasks; highlight and pre-fill. The practical rule: **adaptive in interpretation and presentation, deterministic in decision and implementation**.

**29. What capabilities are prerequisites for agents?**

**[RECOMMENDATION]**

Federated identity with delegation (act “in name” with traceability); authorization at the point of the data (the agent cannot be the last barrier); APIs with contract (tools without API have become fragile automation); explicit processes with owner and exception queue; content governed with indexable permissions; catalogue of services and journeys (without it the agent creates a parallel catalogue); observability and execution record; evaluation set (without it, quality is not measurable); AI policy and data classification.

**30. What technologies are really needed and what are only alternatives?**

**[INFERENCE]**

Needed are *capabilities*: identity with delegation, authorization, APIs with contract, durable processes, governed content, search with permission, protocol of interaction agent-IU, ruled generative UI, tool interface, observability and evaluation. AG-UI or own protocol, A2UI, MCP Apps or own schema, MCP or native calls, Elasticsearch or OpenSearch, Temporal or BPMN are alternatives. Micro-frontends, Kafka, service mesh, dedicated vector bank, multi-agent and full MACH **are not requirements**.

Study **[RECOMMENDATION]**

#### Study trails by profile

The common core, for all, is: the problem, the maturity scale, the layer model and the anti-patterns. The learning goal is to be able to explain the difference between the portal it presents and the platform it solves — and why agents depend on foundations. Then each profile follows where your question lives.

##### Corporate or solution architect

**Read:** architecture, integration, flow, decisions.

**Exercise:** choose a real intention and draw the flow through the layers, marking where they stay rule, state, authorization and audit.

##### Product manager

**Read:** EXP, intent experience, roadmap.

**Exercise:** assemble the ranking of the 20 most frequent intentions (the roadmap phase 0 expands to 50) and classify each by volume, risk and viability.

##### UX or designer service

**Read:** intent experience, generative UI, AG-UI.

**Exercise:** specify three agent components (confirmation, progress, fonts) with when to use, props and accessibility requirements.

##### AI Specialist

**Read:** agents and MCP, search and RAG, knowledge, AG-UI.

**Exercise:** build an evaluation set with 30 real questions, reference documents and groundedness criteria.

##### Platform or SRE

**Read:** operation, front end and streaming, integration and resilience.

**Exercise:** set SLIs and SLOs for an intention, including a quality SLO with error budget and the rape runbook.

##### Content

**Read:** governed content, chain of knowledge, search.

**Exercise:** apply the minimum set of metadata to ten normative and identify gaps in validity, owner and permission.

##### Security and compliance

**Read:** identity and governance, agents and MCP, questions 19 to 30.

**Exercise:** classify ten hypothetical tools by risk and define, for each, scope, level of autonomy and HITL rule.

**Integrator exercise for a multidisciplinary group**

1. Choose a journey (e.g. vacation).
2. Each profile analyzes the journey through the lens itself, alone — as in the architectural board.
3. Consolidate in a matrix of responsibilities between roles (the table of twelve lenses serves as a starting point).
4. Identify conflicts and resolve them with trade-off standards.
5. Position the journey in the maturity model and set the next stage of roadmap.


## Frequently Asked Questions

**What is an agent-oriented Digital Workplace?**

It is an intention-oriented corporate portal and agents: instead of organizing links to systems, it receives the employee's request, prepares the action with an agent, requests confirmation and follows the process to the end. The study describes it as the fifth stage of a maturity model that accumulates the previous: no delegated identity, API contracts, governed content and explicit processes, the agent performs actions with too wide credentials and no audit trail.

**What is an EXP and how does it differ from an intranet?**

Employee Experience Platform (EXP) organizes employee services and journeys on registration systems, with identity, context and delivery across multiple channels. The intranet informs and forwards; the EXP executes and follows. The intranet organizes pages and measures reach; EXP organizes journeys, measures resolution and effort and maintains the state of requests. An EXP does not need to be complicable: what the agent requires is that the capabilities are exposed by contract.

**What is the AG-UI protocol?**

AG-UI (Agent User Interaction Protocol) is an interaction protocol between an agent and the application that the user operates, based on event flows: executions, messages, tool calls, shared state, activity and interruptions for human confirmation. It is not a generic UI specification, it does not integrate corporate systems and does not authorize actions. It complements MCP, which connects agent and tools, and A2A, which connects agents to each other.

**Why doesn't RAG replace content governance?**

Because each link in the chain of knowledge inherits the quality of the former and cannot correct it. The RAG recovers the most similar passage, not the current one or the applicable one: without canonical source, duration, owner and permissions in the index, the answer may come out fluent and wrong. The study recommends six blocking requirements before the RAG and, for actions, the rule that the document explains, but the API decides.

**With what identity should a corporate agent act?**

With delegation, not impersonation: a token obtained by token exchange (RFC 8693) in which the subject is the collaborator and the actor is the agent, with minimum scope and specific audience per tool. The tool server validates the audience and does not pass on the received token; the final authorization should happen at the point of the data, and the “whose” comes from the token, never from parameters generated by the model.

**Where to begin the evolution of a portal to this model?**

The study recommends starting with a high-volume and low-risk pilot journey, not the entire company; vacation and called IT are chances of good drivers, not rule. The roadmap has six phases with passing criteria — discovery, minimum foundations, source responses, agent with reading tools, actions with confirmation, expansion by evidence — and seven parallel tracks. Delegated identity and governed content begin in phase 0 because they are usually the critical path.

## Glossary

- **Agentic Digital Workplace** — Corporate portal that solves intentions through an agent, on foundations of identity, knowledge, APIs and processes; fifth stage of the maturity model.
- **Employment Experience Platform (EXP)** — Layer that organizes employee services and journeys on registration systems, with identity, context and delivery in various channels.
- **AG-UI** — Agent-application interaction protocol, based on event flows, shared status and interruptions; it is neither UI nor integration specification.
- **Component Registry** — Contract between agent and design system: catalogue of approved components, with prop schema, effects and accessibility requirements.
- **Permission-aware retrieval** — Recovery where user permission is filtered in the index before the template sees the content.
- **Delegated identity** — Token in which the subject is the user and the actor is the agent (RFC 8693), so that each action is attributable to both; the study recommends limiting it to the intersection of the permissions of both.
- **Human-in-the-loop (HITL)** — Confirmation or formal human decision before an action with effect, registered as an event and with explicit rule of non-execution if not answered.
- **Agent readiness index** — Score from 0 to 20 of a journey in ten criteria; suggests whether it is ready to work foundations, for RAG and reading or for actions with confirmation.
